title: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a 'significant rise' in AI submissions
key_facts: Google paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program as of 1 Oct 2026.
It promised an update in the first quarter of 2027.
Google blamed a 'significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid'.
Per Tom's Hardware, engineers and maintainers were overwhelmed by invalid reports or ones containing hallucinations.
Participants are told to consider Google's other bug bounty programs.
quote_evidence: This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid.
Google has paused its open source bug bounty program until next year.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-generated low-quality reports are overwhelming vulnerability-reward schemes.
